cross_tool_domains.attrition: High / Serious concern: Constructing a strictly balanced 2015-2019 panel required complete data across all variables and years, excluding roughly 76.6% of Brazilian municipalities that directly provide WWS (retaining 344 municipalities, or 23.4% of direct providers) via complete-unit deletion without missingness diagnostics or statistical adjustment.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High / Serious concern: Municipality and year fixed effects absorb time-invariant municipal heterogeneity and common macro shocks, but logged population (lnPOP) is the sole time-varying covariate retained; unmeasured time-varying fiscal pressures, political changes, intergovernmental grants and differential pre-existing trajectories correlated with cooperation duration (IMCd) remain uncontrolled.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Moderate / Adequate: Participation in horizontal intermunicipal cooperation via public consortia (IMC) and years of participation (IMCd) are operationalized from IBGE's official MUNIC survey (2015-2019), advancing beyond static binary indicators, but the measure does not code underlying consortium contracts, legal mandates or which specific WWS functions are shared.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate concern: Exposure (IBGE MUNIC) and outcome (SNIS) indicators come from independent national administrative surveys using uniform definitions across participating and non-participating municipalities, but both rely on municipal/utility self-reports subject to metering and accounting error.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Moderate / Adequate: Four standardized SNIS indicators capture operational revenue-to-expense ratio (FIN), water coverage (WC), wastewater coverage (WWC) and inverse water-loss index (QUA) over 2015-2019, though SNIS data are utility self-reported and QUA proxies service quality solely through water losses rather than potability, continuity or treatment adequacy.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: No information / Moderate concern: No pre-analysis plan or registered protocol exists to verify pre-specified covariates or outcomes; while fixed-effects, random-effects and Mundlak correlated random-effects estimates are transparently reported for all four outcomes including null and adverse results, preliminary models including GDP per capita and regional controls are mentioned in text without tabulated results.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High / Serious concern: Sample inclusion is restricted to 344 complete-case direct WWS municipalities (6.2% of all Brazilian municipalities; 23.4% of direct providers), and 54 of the 71 IMC municipalities were prevalent participants already cooperating before 2015 (only 17 switched into IMC during 2015-2019), creating complete-case selection and prevalent-user survivorship bias.

domain_ratings.justification: Two-way fixed-effects models (municipality and year fixed effects) and Mundlak correlated random-effects specifications account for time-invariant municipal characteristics and common annual shocks. However, municipal entry into and continuation in public consortia are voluntary political and fiscal decisions, and the final models control only for logged population (lnPOP), omitting time-varying confounders such as local fiscal distress, electoral turnovers, state/federal sanitation transfers and baseline infrastructure shocks (preliminary GDP per capita controls were dropped). Furthermore, IMCd increases by one year per wave for participating municipalities, potentially conflating organizational maturation with differential linear trends among IMC municipalities. As the authors explicitly acknowledge, the estimates capture conditional associations rather than causal effects.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias in selection of participants into the study
domain_ratings.justification: Two selection processes introduce serious risk of bias. First, restricting the sample to a balanced panel with complete data across 2015-2019 retains only 344 municipalities, or 23.4% of Brazilian municipalities that directly provide WWS, likely over-representing administratively stronger providers. Second, among the 71 IMC municipalities in the panel, 54 were prevalent participants already in cooperative arrangements before the 2015 start of follow-up (mean IMCd = 6.92 years, SD = 5.50) and only 17 entered IMC during 2015-2019, introducing prevalent-user and survivorship bias.

Binary participation (IMC) and participation duration in years (IMCd) are drawn from annual waves of IBGE's official Municipal Basic Information Survey (MUNIC, 2015-2019), recorded contemporaneously and independently of SNIS utility outcomes. Nonetheless, the binary and duration measures rely on municipal survey responses without legal-document verification and aggregate potentially heterogeneous consortium arrangements (e.g. joint regulation, procurement or technical operations) into a single exposure category.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_ratings.justification: Routine differences in how public consortia operate across municipalities reflect real-world governance implementation, but the study has no measures of concurrent co-interventions—such as federal or state sanitation grants, tariff restructurings or external technical assistance—that may differentially accompany consortium participation over the 2015-2019 period.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 3-5, Sections 3.1 and 3.2; PDF Page 8, Section 6

domain_ratings.justification: Only 344 municipalities (1,720 observations) had complete data on all study variables across all five years, representing just 23.4% of Brazilian municipalities directly providing WWS. Roughly three-quarters of eligible direct municipal WWS providers were excluded via complete-unit listwise deletion due to missing SNIS or MUNIC data, with no comparison of included versus excluded municipalities and no imputation or weighting adjustments, despite plausible links between SNIS reporting completeness and utility performance.

Financial outcome (FIN), water coverage (WC), wastewater coverage (WWC) and service quality (QUA, inverse water-loss ratio) are obtained from Brazil's standardized National Sanitation Information System (SNIS), an administrative source separate from IBGE MUNIC. Standardized national formulas prevent researcher-driven differential assessment across exposure groups, but SNIS figures are self-reported by local utilities (subject to metering and accounting error, particularly for water losses and expenses) and QUA captures only water losses rather than potability or service continuity.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_ratings.justification: No pre-analysis plan or registered protocol is reported to verify pre-specification of the outcome set, estimator choices or covariate exclusions. While the authors transparently present fixed-effects, random-effects and Mundlak correlated random-effects estimates across all four outcomes (including null and negative coefficients), they state in Section 3.1 that preliminary specifications with GDP per capita and regional controls were estimated and omitted without showing those results.

overall_narrative_summary: Study S448 (Ribeiro et al., 2026) is a comparative longitudinal panel evaluation of 344 Brazilian municipalities that directly provide water and wastewater services (WWS) observed over five years (2015-2019; N = 1,720), examining how participation in intermunicipal cooperation (IMC) via public consortia and duration of cooperation relate to financial balance, water coverage, wastewater coverage and inverse water losses. Appraised with ROBINS-I, the overall risk of bias for causal inference is Serious. Strengths include independent national data sources for governance exposure (IBGE MUNIC) and utility performance (SNIS), separation of cooperation status (IMC) from duration (IMCd), and triangulation across municipality/year two-way fixed-effects, random-effects and Mundlak correlated random-effects estimators. However, three domains carry Serious risk of bias: (D1) logged population is the sole time-varying control, leaving time-varying fiscal distress, political shifts, intergovernmental capital grants and differential linear trajectories correlated with IMCd unadjusted; (D2) 54 of the 71 participating municipalities were already in IMC before 2015 (only 17 entered during the panel), creating prevalent-user survivorship bias alongside complete-case selection; and (D5) requiring complete five-year SNIS and MUNIC records excluded roughly 76.6% of Brazilian municipalities directly providing WWS without missing-data diagnostics or adjustment. Intervention classification (D3), potential co-interventions (D4) and self-reported SNIS outcome measurement (D6) pose Moderate risk of bias, and no pre-analysis plan exists for D7 (No information). The authors appropriately caution that their estimates represent conditional associations rather than definitive causal effects.
study_design_identified: Comparative longitudinal observational panel study (balanced 5-year panel of 344 Brazilian municipalities directly providing water and wastewater services, 2015-2019, N = 1,720 municipality-years) evaluating participation and duration of participation in intermunicipal cooperation (public consortia) using two-way fixed-effects, random-effects and Mundlak correlated random-effects regression models
where_found_summary: Study design, variable definitions, data sources (IBGE MUNIC and SNIS), and sample construction on PDF Pages 3-4 (Section 3.1, Tables 1-2); panel econometric strategy and identification limits (71 IMC municipalities, 17 switchers) on PDF Pages 4-5 (Section 3.2); baseline FE, RE and Mundlak CRE estimates and non-causal caveat on PDF Pages 5-7 (Section 4, Tables 3-6); substantive limitations on PDF Page 8 (Section 6).
why_tool_chosen: The study evaluates a non-randomized municipal governance arrangement/policy—intermunicipal cooperation (IMC) through public consortia—across participating and non-participating Brazilian municipal WWS providers over a 2015-2019 panel using municipality and year fixed-effects, random-effects and Mundlak correlated random-effects estimators. Per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, non-randomized comparative longitudinal/panel policy evaluations with a comparator group map to ROBINS-I.
